questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Myanmar?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Myanmar article.

questions.proof: Its capital city is Naypyidaw and its largest city is Yangon.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Myanmar?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Myanmar on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Myanmar article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by China on the north, Laos on the east, Thailand on the southeast, Bangladesh on the west, and India on the northwest, with the Andaman Sea to the south, and the Bay of Bengal to the southwest.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Myanmar?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “The name, Myamnar” part of the Myanmar article.

questions.proof: The official name of the country in the Burmese language, Myanmar did not change, however.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was occupied by the Empire of _____ in the 1940s.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Empire”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Myanmar article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: It was occupied by the Empire of Japan in the 1940s.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In March _____, Win Myint became the country's tenth President.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Myanmar article, under the heading “History about government”.

questions.proof: In March 2018, Win Myint became the country's tenth President.
